title: Caterpillar power-generation sales up 72% in Q2 as backlog hits USD 72bn, 92% above last year
description: Trefis summarises Caterpillar's Q2 2026 data-centre-driven power-generation growth: retail sales of power generation equipment rose 72% and backlog reached USD 72bn. Management also raised the full-year 2026 sales outlook to mid-to-high teens growth.
quote: The backlog is already huge and stretches years out, so another record order changes little.
analysis: Caterpillar's gensets are being absorbed by hyperscale demand, so its Gulf dealers (Zahid, Al-Bahar) compete for the same constrained factory slots as Cummins Arabia. Action: use Cummins' delivery slots in KSA/UAE data-centre bids as a selling point against Cat dealers' longer allocations (secondary source; confirm against Caterpillar's Q2 release).

title: Caterpillar restarts 10 MW gas engine (1.5 GW capacity), shipments Q4 2026; large gas-engine orders booked into 2028-29
description: Trefis reports Caterpillar is resuming its 10 MW gas engine and plans to bring about 1.5 GW of capacity back online, with shipments expected from Q4 2026. For gas engines used as a site's main power source, the wait for new orders reaches the back half of 2028 into 2029, and some customers order out to 2030.
quote: Some customers of its Power & Energy business are already placing orders as far out as 2030.
analysis: Caterpillar quoting 2028-29 slots for prime-power gas engines is a delivery-time opening for Cummins Arabia on Gulf data-centre and industrial prime-power projects, where owners cannot wait years (our inference; Gulf lead times not verified). Action: price and publish firm Cummins gas/diesel genset delivery windows for KSA/UAE before Cat's 10 MW restart ships in Q4.

title: Caterpillar shares fall 5.75% on 7 Oct; management says turbine orders already extend into 2029-2030
description: FX Leaders reports Caterpillar closed down 5.75% at USD 813.83 on 7 Oct despite a USD 72bn backlog, up 92% year on year. It says growth increasingly comes from large generators for AI data centres, with production of large engines and turbines being increased.
quote: Lately a bigger part of its growth has come from large generators and related gear that power AI data centers.
analysis: Cat is prioritising large data-centre gensets and turbines, which leaves less factory attention for mid-size Gulf standby and prime business that Cummins Arabia serves through its own channels. Action: target mid-size (below 2 MW) standby and rental customers of Cat dealers with shorter-lead-time offers.

title: Caterpillar expects about USD 2.2bn tariff cost in 2026; Q3 results due 29 Oct
description: TradingKey's 8 Oct note flags Caterpillar's projected USD 2.2bn 2026 tariff cost and backlog of USD 72.1bn. It names the 29 October Q3 report as the next catalyst for order momentum and margins.
quote: key risks include high valuation multiples, tariff cost headwinds projected at $2.2 billion for 2026, and execution pressure.
analysis: Tariff cost is a US-cost issue and may support Caterpillar price increases that narrow the price gap to Cummins Arabia; no Gulf price change is reported. Action: re-check Cat dealer price quotes in KSA/UAE after the 29 Oct Q3 call.

title: Caterpillar order surge strains its global manufacturing network, shares near record on data-centre power demand
description: Kalkine reports that data-centre demand for on-site power pushed Caterpillar toward record territory around 11 Oct, with grid-connection delays pushing operators to build their own generation. The surge in orders has tested capacity of Caterpillar's global manufacturing network.
quote: Delivering on a swelling order book depends on a complex global manufacturing network.
analysis: Strained Cat output supports Cummins Arabia's case for Gulf data-centre prime/standby power where delivery dates matter (no figures given in the article, so treat as directional). Action: ask Gulf hyperscale and colocation contacts for their Cat quoted dates and counter with Cummins slots.

title: Caterpillar G3500K gas gensets selected for off-grid Kazakhstan gold mine via dealer Borusan Cat
description: West Gold Mining chose two Cat G3500K gas gensets for a site nearly 300 km from the nearest city in Aktobe, supplied through Cat dealer Borusan Cat. Small in scale, but it shows the G3500K being sold for prime off-grid power.
quote: We needed a power solution that could operate independently off the grid while supporting our long-term plans,
analysis: Cat dealers are positioning G3500K gas sets for remote prime power, the same pitch Gulf dealers can make for remote oil, gas and mining sites in KSA. Action: confirm Cummins Arabia has a comparable gas-genset reference for remote KSA industrial sites.

title: Perkins launches 61-litre V16 5016 genset engine for data centres, says demand 'insatiable'
description: Perkins unveiled the 5016, which tops its 5000 Series (23 to 61 litres, 750 to 2,500 kVA), for backup power at data centres, hospitals and mining. The article cites Skanska expecting generator prices of 100 kW to 4.5 MW to rise 8-10% in 2026 and Perkins saying it has capacity to meet 5000 Series demand.
quote: UK-based engine manufacturer Perkins expects “insatiable” demand from data centre projects, as it launched the diesel-powered 5016 engine
analysis: A 2,500 kVA Perkins engine lets FG Wilson quote larger data-centre sets than before, so it can move into projects where Cummins Arabia's high-kVA sets compete (the article says Perkins has capacity to meet 5000 Series demand). Action: benchmark 5016-based sets (1,400-2,500 kVA, 50 Hz) against Cummins' equivalent on price, load acceptance and lead time.

title: Perkins 5016 enters production: 1,400-2,500 kVA at 50 Hz, runs on 100% HVO, built in Stafford and Aurangabad
description: Perkins' 5016 is in production, completing the 5000 Series at 6, 8, 12 and 16 cylinders, rated up to 2,500 kVA standby and 2,250 kVA prime. It is built for ISO 8528 G3 / NFPA 110 load acceptance, runs on B20 or 100% HVO, and has 750-hour service intervals.
quote: The 61-litre V16 delivers 1400 to 2500 kVA at 50 Hz for base load, prime and standby use.
analysis: 50 Hz rating and 100% HVO capability fit Gulf data-centre specifications, so FG Wilson can quote large 50 Hz sets in KSA/UAE once 5016 sets are available there (Gulf availability not stated). Action: prepare a one-page 5016 comparison for Cummins Arabia's tenders and consultant meetings.

title: Perkins markets 5016 engine for data centres, healthcare, airports and remote sites in Africa and worldwide
description: African Review reports Perkins' 5016 is in production in India and the UK and is offered to Africa and global markets, targeting data centres, healthcare, airports and remote worksites. It uses two smaller turbochargers per bank for load acceptance and takes B20 or 100% HVO.
quote: The 5016 is engineered to offer reliable power at worksites where uptime matters.
analysis: The article names Africa and 'worldwide' but not the Middle East, so Gulf availability of the 5016 is unconfirmed. Action: ask Gulf channel contacts whether FG Wilson and Perkins OEMs have 5016-based sets quoted for KSA/UAE.

title: FG Wilson appoints Green Power International as India distributor, targeting data centres and healthcare
description: GPI (founded 2002, 750+ staff) was named authorised FG Wilson distributor for 40-2,500 kVA diesel sets and lifecycle support in India on 10 Sep. FG Wilson manufactures in India, Brazil and China and sells in over 150 countries.
quote: We are proud to join the FG Wilson distribution network in India.
analysis: This is a paid press release for India, not the Gulf, but it shows FG Wilson adding a data-centre-focused channel and using Indian production capacity that also supplies other export markets. Action: no Gulf change; watch FG Wilson UAE and Saudi distributor announcements (none found in this window).

title: Cummins Inc. says data-centre power demand 'remains robust' as Q2 sales hit record $9.5bn
description: A Motley Fool review of Cummins (published 10 Sep 2026) cites record Q2 2026 revenue of $9.5 billion, full-year growth guidance raised to 10-13%, and Power Systems sales up 19%. It notes the Circe Energy gas-genset deal and a US data-centre BESS selection.
quote: demand for data center power generation remains robust
analysis: Parent demand is strong, but it is led by US, China and Asia Pacific data centres, so large-genset slots compete with Gulf orders. Cummins Arabia should ask Cummins Power Systems for confirmed 2027 allocation on its pipeline of hyperscale sets.

title: Edarat wins SAR 197.8m award for 200MW AI data centre in Saudi Arabia (HUMAIN-MIS development)
description: Edarat received an award letter on 8 Sep 2026 from Al Moammar Information Systems for design, supervision and commissioning of a 200MW AI data centre. The wider HUMAIN-MIS development was raised from 50MW to 250MW and will be delivered in phases.
quote: The development is expected to be delivered in phases.
analysis: A 200MW to 250MW build creates a backup-power requirement of the scale Cummins Arabia already serves (73.2MW hyperscale case study, June 2025). The article names no generator supplier, so approach MIS and Edarat now before the power package is let.

title: Saudi Energy signs three AI data-centre power agreements (HUMAIN Riyadh, center3, Huawei); no MW disclosed
description: On 2 Sep 2026 Saudi Energy announced a grid-electricity agreement for HUMAIN's Riyadh AI data centre, a framework with center3 and an MoU with Huawei. The analysis notes a 14 GW government ambition and a 250MW HUMAIN-MIS build, with no connection dates or values.
quote: The announcements establish coordination, not energised capacity.
analysis: Grid agreements raise the number of sites that will need on-site standby sets, but nothing here is energised capacity or a named generator supplier. Track which of these projects reach power-package tender and map them to Cummins Arabia's Eastern and Central region sales coverage.

title: HUMAIN plans 250 MW online by end-2026 and a 1.7 GW Saudi data-centre build in 2027
description: HUMAIN CEO Tareq Amin said 250 MW comes online by end-2026 and 1.7 GW is built in 2027, rising to about 3 GW by 2030 and 6 GW by 2034. Typical AI data-centre cost is USD 10-12 million per MW.
quote: Almost 80% of my capital is going to the data centers,
analysis: A 1.7 GW build in 2027 is the largest identifiable Saudi demand driver for high-horsepower standby sets, and Cummins Arabia has no public HUMAIN supply deal in the sources checked. Confirm where HUMAIN's EPC and power-package awards stand and secure Cummins QSK78 and QSK60 allocation against them.

title: EquipmentShare and Cummins agree multi-year fleet deal targeting 1 GW of mobile gas power
description: Announced 29 Sep 2026, the agreement makes EquipmentShare a rental and distribution channel for Cummins gas gensets (C1400N6C, 60Hz), with fleet growth to 1 GW for temporary power, microgrid and BESS. The release is US-focused and does not mention the Middle East.
quote: expected fleet growth to 1 gigawatt of natural gas power generation capacity
analysis: It shows Cummins backing a gas-led rental model with large 60Hz units, a template for Saudi mega-project temporary power, where rental is the main route. Review whether Cummins Arabia's rental offering and gas-genset stock can match this, since the product here is 60Hz and the Gulf mostly uses 50Hz.

title: Analyst note: Cummins plans 55 GW capacity by 2030 on about $450m investment, flags data-centre delivery risk
description: A 2 Oct 2026 analysis cites Cummins' plan to add 20 GW for about $450 million, reaching 55 GW by 2030, and data-centre revenue near $5 billion in 2026 guidance. It also cites Goldman Sachs' estimate that 50% to 60% of near-term US data-centre capacity arrives on time.
quote: aligned to visible customer demand.
analysis: More Cummins large-genset capacity eases supply for Gulf customers from 2027-28 but the first additions go to US hyperscalers. Plan Cummins Arabia's 2027 quotes on current lead times and re-check allocation after the Q3 results (estimated 3 Nov 2026, not confirmed).

title: Generac signs long-term Amazon backup-generator supply agreement, issues warrant tied to up to $8bn of payments
description: Generac and Amazon executed a long-term supply agreement on 16 Sep 2026 with initial deliveries of $2.4bn expected in 2027 and 2028. Amazon received a warrant for up to 1,693,745 Generac shares (307,954 vested immediately), with the remainder vesting as gross payments reach up to $8bn.
quote: Initial deliveries of backup generators are expected to total $2.4 billion in 2027 and 2028.
analysis: Generac now has a named, equity-linked hyperscaler customer, which shows a US hyperscaler will tie a generator supplier to itself through 2028. The filing names no Gulf scope, so the direct effect on Cummins Arabia is indirect; ask Cummins global account teams which hyperscalers building in KSA/UAE have framework deals and whether Generac was quoted.

title: Yahoo Finance: Generac up 16% on Amazon deal while Cummins stock unchanged; rally seen as single-supplier event
description: Generac rose about 16% to $203.76 on 17 Sep 2026 after the Amazon deal, Caterpillar rose about 2% to $799.43 and Cummins was flat at $527.48. The article says the $2.4bn signed figure compares with a potential $8bn that Canaccord says could eventually unlock.
quote: a single-customer, single-supplier event rather than a category repricing of standby power
analysis: Markets treated the deal as Generac-specific and did not re-rate Cummins, so there is no investor signal that Cummins' data-centre position is weaker. Use it in Cummins Arabia's data-centre pitch to Gulf operators: Cummins has delivered capacity at scale for years while Generac's volumes are still ramping.

title: Analysis: Amazon $8bn figure is a warrant-vesting threshold, not a guaranteed Generac order
description: TradeVulcan reports the Amazon agreement was signed on 16 Sep 2026 with initial deliveries of $2.4bn in 2027-2028. It stresses that the $8bn is a payment threshold for full warrant vesting and not a committed purchase order.
quote: not a guaranteed $8 billion order
analysis: Only $2.4bn is firm, so headlines of an $8bn Generac order overstate the near-term threat to other suppliers, including Cummins. Brief Cummins Arabia sales not to repeat the $8bn number to customers as a committed volume.

title: Generac targets more than $1.25bn annual large-megawatt generator capacity as Amazon deal lifts attention to scale-up
description: Data Center Frontier reports that Generac expects more than $1.25bn of annual large-megawatt generator manufacturing capacity, with new manufacturing and packaging facilities supporting data-centre deployments. The deal brings initial deliveries of about $2.4bn during 2027 and 2028.
quote: Generac expected to have more than $1.25 billion of annual large-megawatt generator manufacturing capacity
analysis: Added Generac capacity (Q4 2026 target) will compete for the same large diesel genset and enclosure supply chain, while Amazon takes the first slots through 2028. Cummins Arabia should check allocation and lead times for 2-3.5 MW sets with Cummins supply before Gulf data-centre bids in 2027 and quote firm dates.

title: Generac executive: data-centre customers now considering battery energy storage alongside gensets
description: Microgrid Knowledge (10 Sep 2026) profiles Generac's push into the industrial compute age, covering its Illinois packaging site purchase and Enercon enclosure acquisition. A Generac executive says data-centre customers are weighing battery storage to handle erratic AI loads.
quote: We're talking to data centers, where there is more consideration now for battery energy storage.
analysis: Generac is positioning gensets plus BESS and controls as one data-centre package, which is the offer Gulf operators will compare against Cummins. Cummins Arabia should have a genset-plus-BESS reference design ready for UAE and KSA data-centre RFPs.

title: KeyBanc upgrades Generac to Overweight on Amazon contract; Amazon seen as about 1.6bn of 2028 data-centre revenue
description: Goldesel reports on 8 Oct 2026 that KeyBanc analyst Jeffrey Hammond upgraded Generac from Sector Weight to Overweight with a $280 target. It says Amazon is expected to account for about $1.6bn of the $3.0-3.2bn data-centre revenue Generac projects for 2028.
quote: KeyBanc-Analyst Jeffrey Hammond stuft die Generac-Aktie von Sector Weight auf Overweight hoch.
analysis: Generac's 2028 data-centre target of $3.0-3.2bn, with about half from one customer, is mostly a US story and shows limited Gulf exposure. Track whether the share of non-Amazon hyperscalers grows; Cummins Arabia should treat Generac as a Gulf bid rival only once a regional partner is named.

title: Piper Sandler initiates Generac at Overweight ($303); analysts say capacity scale-up is the key question
description: Tradingpedia (8 Oct 2026) reports KeyBanc upgraded Generac and Piper Sandler began coverage at Overweight with a $303 target. Generac has about $4bn of data-centre backlog built in under a year and quarterly revenue is expected to ramp to about $400m from Q3 2027.
quote: the primary question for investors is now centered on Generac's ability to scale capacity
analysis: A roughly $4bn backlog with delivery ramping from Q3 2027 means Generac slots for new customers are likely late 2027 or beyond. Cummins Arabia can use shorter Cummins lead times as a Gulf selling point, once confirmed with Cummins factories; Q3 results (date not yet confirmed) are the next check.

title: Hassan Allam and Sterling & Wilson win US$200m first phase of Humain-center3 Riyadh data centre
description: A joint venture won an estimated SR750m ($200m) contract to build phase one of a Humain and center3 data centre in Riyadh. Phase one has 16.2MW IT load over 16 months, rising to 50MW in phase two, within a wider programme MEED puts at up to 1GW.
quote: The first phase will have an IT load capacity of 16.2MW, with overall capacity reaching 50MW in the second phase.
analysis: A 50MW Riyadh site implies standby/prime generator blocks that will be specified during the 16-month phase-one build, and the EPC pair (Sterling & Wilson is an electrical specialist) is the buying party. Cummins Arabia should open a data-centre power-package conversation with the JV and center3 now, before genset specs are frozen.

title: Microsoft sets November 2026 launch for Saudi Arabia East cloud region
description: Announced at LEAP 2026, the Eastern Province region will have three Azure availability zones and open in November 2026. Microsoft cites an IDC estimate of $44bn new Saudi revenue in 2027-2030, with the region about 13.4% of it.
quote: Located in the Eastern Province, the region will comprise three Azure Availability Zones
analysis: With launch weeks away, the near-term genset value for Cummins Arabia is service, load-bank testing and capacity additions at the Eastern Province sites rather than new-build supply (estimate: construction was reported complete earlier). Pitch O&M and capacity-add upgrades to the facility operators before the November go-live.

title: Saudi new Government Tenders and Procurement Law approved 5 Aug 2026; local-content regime stays in force
description: A Clyde & Co note says the Council of Ministers approved a new GTPL on 5 August 2026 while the 2019 local-content preference rules (10% evaluation price preference for national products, mandatory list) still apply. Contractors face local-content plans, reporting and penalties.
quote: Saudi Arabia has established a comprehensive legal framework governing local content in public procurement.
analysis: Government genset tenders can favour national products by a 10% evaluation preference, which hurts imported brands that lack Saudi content. Cummins Arabia should document its Saudi-assembled or local-content share and check the LCGPA mandatory list for generator sets.

title: Kuwait reviews bids for 3,400MW of power and water PPP projects; contracts possible Q1 2027
description: Joint PPP Authority and MEW committees are evaluating the 1,100MW Shagaya solar phase, a 500MW second Shagaya project and the 1,800MW Al-Khairan IWPP (33 MIGD). If technical evaluations finish by end-2026, contracts could be signed in Q1 2027.
quote: Two international consortia are competing for the project
analysis: These are IPP/IWPP builds with 30 to 54 month schedules, so genset demand is auxiliary and black-start power in 2028-2030, procured by the winning consortium's EPC. Meanwhile Kuwait's supply gap keeps demand for standby and rental power high, so Cummins Arabia's Kuwait rental and standby pipeline should be prioritised ahead of the new-build wave.

title: Hormuz shipping stalls again: five vessels transit in a day, Brent near US$107, Iran offers 7-day reopening plan
description: Kpler data cited by Gulf News show five commodity vessels crossed Hormuz on Saturday 26 Sep versus 31 the prior weekend, with no transits on Sunday. Brent gained about 3% to near $107.30 on 28 Sep.
quote: No transits were recorded on Sunday in the preliminary data.
analysis: Inbound engines, alternators and switchgear for Cummins Arabia in Jebel Ali and Dammam face freight and insurance delays and cost, which can lengthen genset lead times on project deliveries. Review committed delivery dates and safety stock for the data-centre and utility orders due before year end.

title: Hormuz flows recover to about 14m bpd per US, but diesel stays 'very high' and Houthi attack hits Riyadh
description: US Energy Secretary Wright put Gulf crude flows incl. bypass pipelines at 80-90% of pre-war levels, while Kpler showed Hormuz exports at just under 9m bpd in September (44% of February). The article reports a Houthi attack in Riyadh that killed 12 or 13 and injured about 300.
quote: The challenge is still here and the challenge is still ahead of us," he said.
analysis: High diesel prices raise fuel cost for customers running standby and prime sets and push interest toward gas or dual-fuel and bigger storage, while attacks on Riyadh raise the chance of grid and facility hardening demand. Cummins Arabia should prepare a resilience offer (autonomy, fuel storage, dual-fuel) for data-centre, hospital and utility accounts.

title: Al-Mansouria wins US$105m contract to finish 563-bed Taiba University Hospital in Medina
description: A SR396m ($105.6m) contract covers structure, MEP and clinical fit-out for a stalled 563-bed teaching hospital, with three years duration and late-2029 delivery. The original SR500m contract dated from December 2011.
quote: The contract duration is three years, with delivery targeted for late 2029.
analysis: Completion of MEP and medical gas works means hospital standby generation (typically N+1 sets) will be bought by Al-Mansouria's MEP subcontractors within the next 12 to 18 months. Cummins Arabia should contact the contractor and the Medina consultant to be named on the genset spec.

title: Saudi MoD tenders next phase of King Saud Air Base (Hafr Al-Batin); bids due 20 Oct
description: The Ministry of Defence and Aviation is tendering a three-year phase covering headquarters, operations, weapons areas, residential and airfield facilities on a 383 sq km site. First-phase contracts were about SR6.6bn ($1.8bn).
quote: Contractors have been given until 20 October to submit their bids.
analysis: Air bases need prime and standby power and are normally supplied through the winning contractors and military power packages, so the award will set who Cummins Arabia should approach in Q4 2026 or Q1 2027. Identify the bidding teams after 20 October and check Cummins Arabia's military-project references.

title: Houthi strikes on Riyadh's King Khalid airport kill 13; Saudi airport operations suspended
description: MEED reports two weekend strikes on King Khalid International killed 13 and injured 320, with the 10 October terminal strike killing 12. GACA's weekly toll for attacks on Saudi airports is 19 dead and more than 350 injured.
quote: Airport operations were suspended pending a damage assessment.
analysis: Strikes on airports and the capital can delay Riyadh airport and giga-project schedules and staff mobilisation, which pushes back genset deliveries; they also raise demand for hardened standby power at critical sites. Cummins Arabia should check site-access and delivery risk on live Riyadh orders and offer emergency rental sets for damaged facilities.

title: Neom pivots to industry: Oxagon AI data centre breaks ground at 100MW, targeted for 2028
description: MEED says the Oxagon AI data-centre campus broke ground on a first 100MW phase backed by $5bn, targeted for 2028, and that Saudi contract awards reached $68bn so far this year. The $8.5bn Neom green hydrogen plant was commissioned in August.
quote: These developments reflect a kingdom recalibrating rather than retreating
analysis: Demand at Neom is moving from residential giga-project builds to industrial and AI loads, with the 100MW first phase not live until 2028, so genset orders come late and via the data-centre developer and EPC. Cummins Arabia should reposition its Neom account from MEP packages to the Oxagon AI campus and track the EPC award.

title: Diriyah awards US$729m of hotel and residential contracts to UCC Saudi and a local JV
description: Diriyah Company awarded two contracts worth more than SR2.7bn ($729m): $375m to UCC Saudi and $353m to a Almajal Alarabi / Man Enterprise Al-Saudia JV for hotels and branded residences. Scope includes MEP and fit-out in Diriyah Square.
quote: The Diriyah masterplan envisages the city as a cultural and lifestyle tourism destination.
analysis: Hotel and residential towers need standby generation, specified during the MEP phase that the two awarded contractors are starting. Cummins Arabia should approach both MEP packages with a standard hospitality genset offer.

title: Kuwait tenders 24-inch gas export pipeline from BS-171; bids due 5 January 2027
description: A tender covers a 24-inch gas export line from the BS-171 acid-gas facility, about 80 km to the ISC facility. A preliminary online meeting is set for mid-November.
quote: The bid deadline is 5 January 2027.
analysis: A pipeline contract carries small remote-site power needs, but it signals continued Kuwaiti upstream spending despite the conflict. Add it to the Kuwait oil and gas watch list and brief the bidding contractors on Cummins Arabia's field-power and service offer.

title: Six contractor groups prequalify for AED34bn Dubai Metro Gold Line
description: Six consortiums submitted prequalification statements on 9 October for the fully underground 42km, 18-station line, costed at about AED34bn ($9.2bn), with completion targeted for September 2032.
quote: The project is scheduled to be completed in September 2032.
analysis: An underground metro needs emergency and tunnel-ventilation backup power at 18 stations, but orders are 2028 onwards and sit with the winning consortium's MEP contractors. Cummins Arabia should map the six consortium members now and engage the favourites before the tender stage.

title: Kuwait approves KD5.52m of high-voltage cable maintenance to protect summer 2027 peak
description: Kuwait's electricity ministry cleared two high-voltage transformer cable maintenance and repair projects worth KD5.52m in the northern and southern regions. The work targets summer 2027 and aims to reduce outage risk at peak demand.
quote: The work is also intended to reduce the risk of outages during periods of peak demand.
analysis: With no large new generation online before 2027-28 and a stressed grid, Kuwaiti commercial and industrial customers keep relying on standby and rental gensets through summer 2027. Cummins Arabia should build rental and standby capacity in Kuwait before April 2027.

title: Al-Yamama wins infrastructure contract for Humain's 6GW east Riyadh AI data centre campus
description: Humain awarded Al-Yamama Trading & Contracting the infrastructure package for a 6GW hyperscale campus on a 24 sq km site in Al-Saad, east Riyadh, on an early-contractor-involvement basis. Scope includes a 2,000MVA bulk supply point, 500MVA and 200MVA substations and 380kV/132kV/33kV distribution; the value was not disclosed.
quote: The development will be built on a 24-square-kilometre site in the Al-Saad area in east Riyadh.
analysis: A 6GW campus is the largest data-centre power opportunity in the Gulf, and the ECI route means backup-power concepts are set early with the contractor and Humain rather than at a later tender. Cummins Arabia should open a technical dialogue with Humain and Al-Yamama now on standby and bridging power for the first halls.

title: Combined Group wins KD9.7m KOC five-year repair and revamp contract for West Kuwait production facilities
description: Kuwait Oil Company awarded Combined Group Contracting a KD9.7m (about $31.6m) five-year contract to repair, rehabilitate and revamp existing production facilities in West Kuwait.
quote: Combined Group Contracting will undertake the required repair and revamping works for production facilities
analysis: A five-year revamp of existing KOC facilities means recurring replacement of emergency and utility generators and spares, which is service and aftermarket business rather than new-build supply. Cummins Arabia should offer Combined Group a framework for genset replacement and overhaul on the West Kuwait sites.

title: Saudi power contract awards fall to US$3.38bn in 2026 as SPPC moves to storage; 3GW storage bids due October
description: MEED Projects says Saudi power awards total $3.38bn so far in 2026 against $27.5bn in 2025, with transmission $3.35bn of it. SPPC awarded four storage agreements (2,000MW, 8,000MWh) and has six more storage projects (3GW, 12,000MWh) with bids due in October.
quote: has seen a sharp fall in contract awards in 2026.
analysis: New thermal plant awards that carry black-start and auxiliary genset packages have slowed, and the pipeline is solar, wind and batteries, which need little genset capacity. Cummins Arabia should shift Saudi utility effort toward the storage and transmission substation contractors and toward SEC service work.

title: UAE raises October diesel price to Dh4.80 a litre, up 11.6% from September
description: The UAE Fuel Price Committee set diesel at Dh4.80 a litre for October 2026 against Dh4.30 in September. Gulf News says all fuel grades rose from 1 October as global oil prices stay elevated.
quote: Diesel: Dh4.80 a litre, up from Dh4.30 — 11.6% increase
analysis: Higher diesel raises the running cost of prime and rental sets and strengthens the case for gas or dual-fuel and for efficient fuel-saving controls in customer proposals. Cummins Arabia should add fuel-cost scenarios at Dh4.80 per litre to rental and prime-power quotes this quarter.

title: UAE freight group says cost of shipping into the Gulf is three to five times earlier levels, mostly surcharges
description: The UAE National Association of Freight and Logistics says total cost of moving cargo into the Gulf has risen to roughly three to five times earlier levels. Basic ocean freight has not risen by the same factor; war-risk, emergency and fuel surcharges and rerouting drive the increase.
quote: the sharp increase largely reflected the accumulation of additional charges associated with transporting containers.
analysis: Inbound engines, alternators and switchgear carry surcharges that squeeze margin on fixed-price genset contracts, and competitors with Gulf-based assembly or stock are less exposed. Cummins Arabia should review open fixed-price quotations for freight clauses and hold stock of fast-moving standby models.

title: Kuwait: Kaifan substation fault cuts power to parts of Hawalli and Mubarak Al-Kabeer
description: A technical fault at the Kaifan (B) main substation took five secondary feeders out of service on 6 September, cutting power in parts of Hawalli and Mubarak Al-Kabeer. The ministry did not say which areas or how many customers were affected.
quote: Emergency teams were dispatched to the site and were working to restore electricity as quickly as possible.
analysis: Localised feeder failures after a summer of conflict damage keep commercial and healthcare sites in Kuwait dependent on standby sets, even though this one fault was small. Cummins Arabia should follow up its Kuwait standby and rental accounts in the affected governorates.

title: Kuwait Gulf Oil Company fast-tracks US$3.3bn Dorra gas processing plant tender near Al-Zour; bids due 29 Dec
description: The onshore plant near the Al-Zour refinery is sized for up to 632 million cf/d of gas and 60,000 b/d of condensate from the offshore Dorra field in the Saudi-Kuwaiti Neutral Zone. The contractor meeting moved from 14 September to 14 October and at least seven international EPC firms are reported interested.
quote: The tender was floated last month, with December 29, 2026 set as the deadline for receiving bids.
analysis: A plant of this size will need emergency, black-start and construction power, bought by the winning EPC (Samsung E&A, L&T and JGC are named as interested), with award not before 2027. Cummins Arabia should register with the interested EPC firms before the 14 October contractor meeting and offer construction-phase rental power.

title: AWS plans first Saudi cloud region for December and 50MW Humain AI Zone by 2028; Saudi data-centre capacity above 467MW
description: The National reports AWS's first Saudi region launches in December with planned investment above $5.3bn, and AWS and Humain plan up to 50MW in a dedicated AI Zone by 2028. Saudi operational data-centre capacity rose from 68MW in 2021 to more than 467MW, with Humain targeting about 6GW by 2034.
quote: It comes as Gulf nations are increasing investment in the infrastructure needed to support an AI-driven economy.
analysis: Saudi data-centre capacity has grown nearly sevenfold since 2021, and a December AWS launch means commissioning, load testing and service work in the next 90 days. Cummins Arabia should target the AWS region's operators for service contracts and the Humain AI Zone for new standby capacity.

title: AWS says it cannot restore one of its three UAE availability zones after war damage
description: AWS told customers it cannot restore access to resources and data hosted exclusively in the damaged UAE and Bahrain zones, and says most customers re-established operations in other regions. No timeline was given for the UAE zone.
quote: We have determined that we are unable to restore access to the resources and data hosted exclusively
analysis: Operators now treat physical resilience of power, cooling and site hardening as a design requirement, and a rebuild or replacement of a lost UAE zone would create genset demand (the article does not say power was the cause, so this is an inference). Cummins Arabia should offer hardened, redundant standby power and fast-response service to UAE colocation and hyperscale operators.

title: Saudi water-sector awards fall to US$3.94bn in 2026 with no major desalination award; Riyadh East ISTP bids due 29 Sep
description: MEED Projects shows Saudi water awards at $3.94bn by early September against $10.7bn in 2025, led by Aramco ($2.15bn) and NWC ($1.09bn). No major desalination or storage contract has been awarded, and the $2bn Riyadh-Qassim transmission pipeline developer agreement is unsigned.
quote: The slowdown in awards appears to reflect the timing of projects moving through procurement
analysis: Water awards are concentrated in treatment plants and Aramco, so genset demand is driven by few buyers while desalination awards (large standby and auxiliary power) are still pending. Cummins Arabia should prioritise NWC and Aramco-linked treatment contractors now and prepare for the desalination awards when they come.

title: Iran steps up tanker attacks around Hormuz: at least 12 tankers hit in a week, a drone strike 25km off UAE's Al Jazeera
description: At least 12 tankers were attacked in and around Hormuz between 28 Sep and 5 Oct, and UKMTO reported six vessels struck on Sunday 11 Oct including a container ship. The crude carrier Gem No 2 was hit by a drone about 25 km west of Al Jazeera in the UAE.
quote: The Strait of Hormuz is closed and the armed forces of the Islamic Republic of Iran have full control over it.
analysis: A container ship among the vessels hit means genset, engine and alternator imports into Gulf ports face delay and surcharge risk through the Q4 delivery window. Cummins Arabia should confirm routing via Jeddah, Dammam or Khor Fakkan for committed deliveries and warn key project customers of schedule risk.

title: Houthi drone hits Taiba power distribution station in Madinah, UAE condemns
description: The UAE foreign ministry condemned a Houthi drone attack on the Taiba power distribution station in Madinah, and the Saudi-led coalition said the station was hit by a drone.
quote: this attack constitutes a flagrant violation of the sovereignty of Saudi Arabia.
analysis: Attacks on Saudi grid assets raise the value of on-site standby power for hospitals, pilgrim facilities and utilities in Madinah and show the need for emergency rental sets for grid repair. Cummins Arabia should pre-position rental units and a service team in the Western Region and brief Saudi Energy and municipal accounts.

title: Kuwait starts periodic grid maintenance from 1 October ahead of next summer, warns of temporary outages
description: The Ministry of Electricity, Water and Renewable Energy began periodic maintenance of the transmission and distribution network, from main stations to secondary substations, to reduce emergency faults. It warned of temporary outages and will notify customers through the Sahl platform.
quote: may result in temporary power interruptions in some areas
analysis: Planned outages during maintenance create short-term demand for temporary and rental generation at commercial and industrial sites in Kuwait. Cummins Arabia should contact Kuwait rental customers with the published outage schedules and offer short-term cover.

title: Clyde & Co: Saudi's new tenders law lifts direct-purchase limit to SR1m and variation cap to 20%; localisation rules still to come
description: Clyde & Co's 1 October overview says the direct purchase threshold rises from SAR 100,000 to SAR 1 million, the cap on contract variations rises from 10% to 20%, and industrial localisation rules will follow in a separate framework. The statutory text and implementing regulations had not yet been published.
quote: The direct purchase threshold increases from SAR 100,000 to SAR 1 million.
analysis: A SAR 1m direct-purchase limit lets government entities buy small and mid-size gensets, spares and service without open tender, which favours suppliers already known to the buyer. Cummins Arabia should refresh its registrations with ministries and agencies and watch the pending localisation framework that may add a local-content preference.

title: Five consortiums bid for US$150m Riyadh East sewage treatment plant, including Marafiq-led group; bids received 28 September
description: Sharakat received bids on 28 September for the 200,000 m3/d phase one (500,000 m3/d phase two) Riyadh East ISTP, a 25-year BOT valued at $150m, with commercial operation targeted for 2029. Bidders include EtihadWE/Metito, GS Inima/Alkhorayef, Lamar/China Harbour, Miahona/Marafiq/Bin Omairah and Suez/Civil Works/Alwael.
quote: Bids were submitted on 28 September.
analysis: Sewage treatment plants need standby generation for pumping and aeration, bought by the winning developer's EPC contractor after a 2027 award (estimate), so the sets are modest but repeat across Sharakat's ISTP programme. Cummins Arabia should map the five consortium EPC partners and offer a standard ISTP standby package.

title: Rolls-Royce licenses MAKEEN to build mtu Series 2000 engines in Saudi Arabia, first high-speed engine licence in the Kingdom
description: Rolls-Royce Power Systems signed an Individual License Agreement with Saudi Engines Manufacturing Company (MAKEEN; Aramco, HD Hyundai, Dussur) for local manufacture and assembly of mtu Series 2000 marine engines (up to 1,939 kW), building on a November 2023 framework agreement. No volumes, investment or start date are disclosed; rail is named as the next target after marine.
quote: Saudi Arabia is investing heavily in industrial development, infrastructure and energy projects.
analysis: This is a marine and rail engine licence, not a genset or data-centre deal, so it does not hit Cummins Arabia's standby power sales today. It does show Rolls-Royce building a local-content position with Aramco-linked partners in KSA, which can later help mtu in localisation-scored power tenders. Action: ask the KSA team to track whether MAKEEN's scope extends from Series 2000 to Series 4000 genset engines, and to prepare Cummins' own local-content evidence for Saudi tenders.

title: Energy Vault contracts 275 MW of Rolls-Royce mtu engine capacity for hyperscale AI sites, deliveries H2 2027 to H1 2028
description: Energy Vault announced on 10 Sep 2026 that it secured and fully contracted 275 MW of reciprocating engine generation capacity using Rolls-Royce mtu technology, financed by Eagle Point Credit Management. Deliveries start in the second half of 2027 and run through the first half of 2028.
quote: Equipment deliveries are expected to begin in the second half of 2027 and continue through the first half of 2028.
analysis: Third-party buyers are now reserving mtu engine slots 15 to 21 months out for AI and hyperscale power, which shows mtu output for 2027 to 2028 is being absorbed by US demand. That limits how much mtu capacity is free for Gulf data-centre bids in the same window, which supports Cummins' delivery-time argument. Action: quote firm Cummins delivery slots in Gulf data-centre proposals and compare them against mtu's 2027 to 2028 availability.

title: Rolls-Royce opens mtu Remote Monitoring Centre in Arcola, Italy, covering power generation plants as well as marine
description: Rolls-Royce commissioned a Remote Monitoring Centre in Arcola, Italy, the first outside Berlin, for vessels with mtu engines and for power generation plants, starting with marine and yacht fleets. Regional Remote Monitoring Hubs are planned, and the company calls it the start of a global roll-out.
quote: The mtu Go platform provides the technological basis for remote monitoring.
analysis: No Gulf centre is named, and the first customers are Italian marine users, so there is no near-term effect on Cummins Arabia. A regional monitoring hub for mtu power plants would strengthen the service offer of mtu distributors such as Al Mulla in Kuwait. Action: check that Cummins Arabia's remote-monitoring offer for data-centre and hospital customers matches this, and watch for a Middle East hub.

title: Rehlko doubles Changzhou backup-power capacity from 5.5 GW to 11 GW; plant ships to EMEA
description: Rehlko is raising annual backup power capacity at its Changzhou plant in China from 5.5 GW to 11 GW without extending the footprint, and says first pass yield rose from 93% to 98%. The plant makes gensets from 6 kW to 4,000 kW and serves China, Southeast Asia, EMEA and Latin America; Rehlko cites more than 14 GW of data-centre capacity deployed to date.
quote: Our continued investments at Changzhou reflect the discipline behind our growth, doubling capacity while sharpening the speed and precision behind every system we ship
analysis: EMEA is a named market for Changzhou, so Rehlko can supply Gulf distributors with more units from a lower-cost base and may offer shorter lead times and sharper prices on mid-range and large standby sets. Action: benchmark Rehlko KD Series pricing and delivery quotes in recent UAE and Saudi data-centre bids and brief the sales team on how to respond.

title: Trade analysis: data-centre diesel genset lead times 18-24 months above 2.5 MW, naming Caterpillar, Cummins and Kohler order books
description: A Datacentres.com research note dated 3 Sep 2026 puts diesel generator lead times at 18 to 24 months for units above 2.5 MW, citing OEM order books at Caterpillar, Cummins and Kohler. It expects the constraint to remain binding through at least 2027.
quote: diesel generator lead times stretch to 18-24 months for units above 2.5 MW, according to OEM order books at Caterpillar, Cummins and Kohler
analysis: Long industry lead times favour a supplier that can hold slots, and Cummins Arabia is named in the same order-book set as Rehlko (Kohler). The note is a US-led global estimate and does not mention Rolls-Royce mtu or the Gulf, so treat the figures as indicative. Action: confirm Cummins Arabia's actual lead times for 2 to 4 MW sets with the factory and use them in data-centre proposals.

title: Generac signs Amazon backup-generator supply deal worth up to USD 8bn
description: Generac signed a long-term supply agreement to provide backup generators for Amazon data centres, with initial deliveries of about USD 2.4bn across 2027 and 2028 and milestones extending up to USD 8bn of payments. Amazon received a warrant for up to 1,693,745 Generac shares tied to payments received.
quote: Initial deliveries under the agreement are expected to total approximately $2.4 billion during 2027 and 2028.
analysis: A hyperscaler locking a large-megawatt genset supplier into 2027-28 slots tightens global supply of data-centre sets and signals Generac is now a credible large-genset rival. Cummins Arabia should confirm its own 2027-28 slot allocation for Gulf hyperscale projects and use any lead-time advantage in current bids.

title: Cummins and EquipmentShare plan 1 GW natural-gas mobile power fleet using C1400N6C sets
description: EquipmentShare and Cummins announced a multi-year collaboration, with EquipmentShare's fleet expected to grow to 1 GW of natural-gas generation. The core unit is the Cummins C1400N6C, a 60 Hz continuous lean-burn gas set of 1400-1750 kVA.
quote: the C1400N6C, a 60Hz continuous lean burn gas generator set capable of delivering between 1400 - 1750 kVA of power
analysis: Cummins is placing large continuous-duty gas sets through a rental channel, which validates gas gensets as prime power and pulls factory output toward US rental. Cummins Arabia should ask Cummins for C1400N6C-class gas availability for Gulf prime-power and rental customers before the US fleet absorbs the slots.

title: Rehlko redesigns KG Series gas gensets, six EPA-certified models of 80-200 kW at 60 Hz
description: Rehlko introduced six redesigned KG Series gaseous generators (KG80 to KG200) for 60 Hz standby use, on 6.2 L and 10.3 L Rehlko engines with a 2-year warranty extendable to 5 years. Target sites include healthcare, water treatment and telecom.
quote: Rehlko is strengthening its KG Series gaseous generator portfolio with six EPA-certified models for 60 Hz applications
analysis: This is a small-set, US-emissions-certified 60 Hz range, below Cummins Arabia's data-centre core, so direct Gulf impact is limited and applies only to the 60 Hz parts of KSA. Cummins Arabia should check whether Rehlko dealers in KSA start quoting KG gas sets for hospital and water-utility standby.

title: Caterpillar supplies two Cat G3500K island-mode gas gensets to a Kazakhstan gold mine
description: Caterpillar, through dealer Borusan Cat, is supplying two Cat G3500K gas generator sets in a containerised enclosure to an off-grid gold mine in Aktobe, about 300 km from the nearest city. Operating range is -30C to above 30C and a Customer Value Agreement is planned after commissioning.
quote: The Cat G3500K gas power solution is designed to operate in island mode independent from the grid
analysis: Cat is packaging gas gensets with a service agreement for off-grid sites, the same offer Gulf dealers can take to remote mining, giga-project and camp power. Cummins Arabia should price a matching gas-plus-service package for KSA off-grid and mining prospects.

title: Perkins to show 5016 large electronic-injection genset engine at Tech Week Singapore 2026
description: Perkins said it will exhibit the 5016 large electronic fuel injection engine at Tech Week Singapore 2026 (stand L20), positioning the sets for data centres, power stations, rental and hospitals. The release gives no kVA, emissions or availability figures.
quote: This series of generator sets is widely deployed in data centers, power stations, rental applications and hospitals
analysis: Perkins keeps pushing the 5016 (FG Wilson sets) as a data-centre option at the upper end of its range, a price-led alternative in Gulf colocation and edge sites. Cummins Arabia should compare 5016-based FG Wilson quotes against its own 1.5-2.5 MVA offers on current bids.

title: Wärtsilä books 282 MW US data-centre onsite plant on 15 Wärtsilä 50SG gas engines
description: Wärtsilä will supply 15 Wärtsilä 50SG engines for a 282 MW onsite power plant at a US data centre, delivery in 2028 and full operation in 2029. It is Wärtsilä's seventh US data-centre order, taking sold US data-centre capacity above 3 GW.
quote: The Wärtsilä equipment is scheduled for delivery in 2028, and the project is expected to become fully operational in 2029.
analysis: Engine plants are being booked 2-3 years out for data-centre prime power, which shows how far gas capacity is sold forward and why delivery slots now decide awards. Cummins Arabia should treat 2028 delivery as the benchmark when quoting Gulf data-centre gas or diesel sets.

title: Wärtsilä, Schneider Electric and Stanley Consultants launch 'generator-to-chip' data-centre power offer
description: The three companies introduced a coordinated approach combining onsite engine generation, electrical infrastructure and engineering to speed US data-centre power delivery. Wärtsilä supplies modular engine plants, Schneider the electrical and digital power management.
quote: For many data center projects, power has become the schedule.
analysis: Engine makers are bundling generation, switchgear and controls into one delivery package, which competes with a genset-only supplier on schedule. Cummins Arabia should offer Gulf hyperscale customers a comparable package (sets, paralleling switchgear, controls, commissioning) with one delivery date.

title: Trina Storage previews gas-plus-battery 'Elementa Hybrid Genset' for AI data centres
description: Trina Storage showed a platform pairing a gas-fired plant with grid-forming containerised batteries so a data centre can energise without a utility connection. Commercial launch is planned at RE+ 2026 in Las Vegas.
quote: Trina expects to launch this hybrid platform commercially at RE+2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada.
analysis: Battery makers are entering the genset space with grid-forming BESS that rides fast load swings, which could shrink the number of gensets specified per hall. Cummins Arabia should be ready with its own genset-plus-BESS option (Cummins announced on 18 Aug it was selected to supply BESS for a US data-centre project) for Gulf prime-power tenders.

title: 2G Energy wins 275 MW order from Energy Vault for US AI-infrastructure power systems
description: 2G Energy AG received a 275 MW order from Energy Vault for containerised power systems for AI and data-centre customers including hyperscalers. Delivery runs Q4 2027 to Q3 2028 and 2G is building a second production site at Heek, Germany, due end-2027.
quote: Through long-term service, we also support their reliable operation throughout the entire lifecycle.
analysis: Another gas-engine supplier is committing its output to US AI sites into late 2028, which adds to the tightness in packaged gas gensets. Cummins Arabia should expect gas-set lead times to stay long and flag this to Gulf prime-power prospects early.
